about: Edges of slice 0 (pensions + public finances) of /visualizaciones/sistema/. Each item says exactly what number the model needs and how it is used. Model: annual steps 2026-2050, deviations from the Ageing Report 2024 baseline for Spain (current law: CPI indexation, MEI, 2023 reform).

parameter.name: lambda_renovacion
parameter.unit: fracción del stock de pensiones por año

items.need: Annual share of the stock of contributory pensions in force that is replaced: new pensions (altas iniciales) per year / pensions in force, Spain, average 2022-2024 (also give bajas / stock). Model use: an extra real revaluation r applies to the whole stock each year, while new pensions enter without it, so the average pension deviation x follows x_t = (1-lambda)(x_{t-1}+r).
items.hints: Seguridad Social, eSTADISS / Boletín de Estadísticas Laborales (pensiones contributivas: altas, bajas, en vigor); Informe Económico-Financiero de los Presupuestos de la Seguridad Social.

parameter.name: kappa_cohorte
parameter.unit: fracción de pensionistas por año de edad

items.need: Share of all public pensioners (persons) that one year of retirement age represents: new retirement pensions (altas de jubilación) per year / total pensioners. Model use: +1 year of effective retirement age removes about kappa of pensioners (phased in), times the share of retirement pensions taken at or near the ordinary age. ALSO give, in derivation and value_in_source, the average monthly amount of NEW retirement pensions (altas de jubilación, régimen general) vs the average of ALL pensions in force, as a ratio (put it in extra_parameters as new_pension_relative).
items.hints: Seguridad Social altas de jubilación por edad (eSTADISS), number of pensioners; AR2024 country fiche Spain gives pensioners 10.24 M in 2024.

parameter.name: permanencia_empleo
parameter.unit: fracción de la cohorte retrasada que sigue ocupada

items.need: When the retirement age rises by one year, which share of the affected cohort stays employed (vs moves to disability/unemployment benefits or inactivity without pension). Give also the spillover share to other benefits (for the card's derivation). Put the share of the delayed cohort that moves to OTHER public benefits (disability, unemployment) times the relative cost of those benefits vs a pension in extra_parameters as prestacion_alternativa (fraction of the avoided pension cost that reappears as other benefits).
items.hints: Staubli & Zweimüller (2013, J Public Econ, Austria); Spanish evidence on the 2011/2013 reforms (Banco de España, FEDEA, AIReF); Seibold (2021, AER) on statutory ages; Rabaté et al.

parameter.name: tipo_marginal_irpf_pension
parameter.unit: fracción de cada euro extra de pensión

items.need: IRPF marginal rate (state + regional) on an extra euro of pension for the average pensioner (about 21,700 EUR gross per year), and the average effective rate on pension income overall. Model use: net fiscal cost of extra pension = gross cost x (1 - rate).
items.hints: AEAT Estadística de declarantes del IRPF (rendimientos del trabajo: pensiones); IRPF scale 2024-2025 (19 / 24 / 30 %); OECD Pensions at a Glance (net vs gross).

parameter.name: multiplicador_transferencias
parameter.unit: euros de PIB por euro de transferencia, primer año

items.need: First-year GDP multiplier of transfers to households for Spain (normal times), and its persistence (how much remains in year 2 and 3). Model use: output deviation = multiplier x change in transfers, decaying. ALSO report, in the derivation and an extra source if needed, the first-year multiplier of increases in labour taxes/social contributions and in VAT for Spain (model uses one tax multiplier; put them in extra_parameters as multiplicador_impuestos and persistencia_multiplicador).
items.hints: Banco de España (de Castro, Martí, Montesinos, Pérez, Sánchez-Fuentes 2017 'Fiscal multipliers in Spain'); EC QUEST; IMF; Coenen et al. 2012.

parameter.name: semielasticidad_saldo
parameter.unit: pp del PIB de saldo por 1 % de PIB

items.need: Budget balance semi-elasticity to the output gap for Spain (EU commonly agreed methodology).
items.hints: Mourre, Poissonnier & Lausegger (2019, European Economy Discussion Paper 100); Price, Dang & Botev (2014, OECD WP 1174).

parameter.name: traslado_cotizacion_salario
parameter.unit: fracción del aumento de cotización empresarial que acaba en menor salario, largo plazo

items.need: Long-run share of an employer social-contribution increase that is shifted to workers through lower gross wages (incidence). This is contested: give each school (full shifting vs little shifting) with its source; prefer Spanish or EU evidence.
items.hints: Gruber (1997, Chile); Saez, Schoefer & Seim (2019, AER, Sweden); Bozio, Breda & Grenet (France); Kugler & Kugler (2009, Colombia); Melguizo & González-Páramo (2013, meta-analysis); Spanish evidence on contribution reductions (tarifa plana, bonificaciones).

parameter.name: elasticidad_empleo_coste
parameter.unit: % de empleo por 1 % de coste laboral, largo plazo

items.need: Long-run constant-output or total own-wage elasticity of labour demand, preferably meta-analytic plus Spanish estimates. Model use: employment deviation = elasticity x labour-cost deviation (negative number).
items.hints: Lichter, Peichl & Siegloch (2015, European Economic Review, meta-analysis); Hamermesh (1993); Spanish estimates (Banco de España, FEDEA).

parameter.name: base_cotizacion_pib
parameter.unit: % del PIB recaudado por 1 pp de tipo de cotización

items.need: Revenue from 1 percentage point of contribution rate on the general contribution base, in % of GDP (e.g. derived from the official MEI yield: 0.6 pp raised X million EUR in 2023 or 2024 / nominal GDP).
items.hints: Seguridad Social / Ministerio de Inclusión (recaudación MEI, Fondo de Reserva dotaciones); AIReF opinions on the 2023 reform; nominal GDP from INE.

parameter.name: recaudacion_por_1pct_empleo
parameter.unit: % del PIB de ingresos públicos por 1 % de empleo

items.need: Public revenue (IRPF on wages + social contributions) lost when employment falls 1 % at the average wage, plus unemployment benefit cost, in % of GDP. Derive from labour tax revenue in % of GDP (OECD Revenue Statistics / Eurostat gov_10a_taxag, Spain 2023-2024) and unemployment benefit coverage.
items.hints: Eurostat gov_10a_taxag (D61 contributions, D51 income tax), OECD Taxing Wages tax wedge for Spain, SEPE coverage rate.

parameter.name: recaudacion_por_punto_iva
parameter.unit: % del PIB por 1 pp del tipo general

items.need: Static VAT revenue from raising the standard VAT rate by 1 pp, in % of GDP, and the behavioural/compliance offset if estimated (the 2012 hike 18->21 % is a Spanish test).
items.hints: AEAT Informe Anual de Recaudación 2012-2013 (efecto de la subida de tipos); AIReF; Ministerio de Hacienda memoria de beneficios fiscales; EC VAT gap reports.

parameter.name: traslado_iva_precios
parameter.unit: fracción del cambio de tipo trasladada a precios de consumo

items.need: Pass-through of a standard-rate VAT change to consumer prices, and the share of the HICP basket taxed at the standard rate in Spain. Spanish 2012 evidence preferred (INE IPC a impuestos constantes).
items.hints: Benedek, De Mooij, Keen & Wingender (2020, Int Tax Public Finance); INE IPC a impuestos constantes (IPC-IC) September 2012; Banco de España notes on the 2012 hike.

parameter.name: indiciacion_salarios
parameter.unit: fracción de un aumento del IPC trasladada a salarios en 1-2 años

items.need: Share of a one-off price-level increase that wages recover within 1-2 years in Spain (coverage of wage-guarantee clauses in collective agreements, estimates of wage response to inflation).
items.hints: Ministerio de Trabajo, Estadística de Convenios Colectivos (cláusula de garantía salarial); Banco de España Informe Anual / boletines 2022-2024 on wage indexation; AENC V.

parameter.name: indiciacion_pensiones_ipc
parameter.unit: fracción del IPC (Dic-Nov) aplicada al año siguiente

items.need: Legal rule: Ley 21/2021 revaluation with the average year-on-year CPI December-November of the previous year; timing (lag of one year) and any compensation clause. Model use: a price rise in year t raises pensions in t+1 by the same %.
items.hints: BOE Ley 21/2021 (art. 58 LGSS as amended), BOE-A-2021-21652.

parameter.name: prima_por_deuda
parameter.unit: puntos básicos de tipo a largo plazo por 1 pp de deuda/PIB

items.need: Increase in long-term government bond yields per percentage point of debt/GDP (euro area / Spain).
items.hints: Laubach (2009, JEEA); European Commission Debt Sustainability Monitor (assumption on interest-rate effect of debt); ECB papers; Banco de España.

parameter.name: cuota_refinanciacion
parameter.unit: fracción de la deuda que se refinancia o emite cada año

items.need: Average residual maturity of Spanish State debt (Tesoro Público) in years and the implied annual share of debt repriced (gross financing needs / debt). Model use: implicit rate moves toward the market rate by this share each year.
items.hints: Tesoro Público, Estrategia de Financiación 2025 (vida media), Boletín mensual; AIReF debt monitor.

parameter.name: mei_tipo_2029
parameter.unit: pp de la base de cotización

items.need: Legislated MEI (Mecanismo de Equidad Intergeneracional) rate path from 2023 to 2050 and its employer/worker split (RDL 2/2023), plus official revenue in EUR for one year.
items.hints: BOE RDL 2/2023 (BOE-A-2023-6967); Seguridad Social press/AIReF on MEI revenue.

parameter.name: coste_revalorizacion_2023
parameter.unit: millones de euros, primer año

items.need: BENCHMARK for a backtest: official estimate of the cost of the 8.5 % revaluation of 2023 (contributory + non-contributory), in million EUR, and pension spending of 2022 it applies to.
items.hints: Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones press release Dec 2022; Presupuestos 2023; AIReF.

parameter.name: perdida_poder_adquisitivo_irp
parameter.unit: % de la pensión real perdida acumulada 2014-2018 frente al IPC

items.need: BENCHMARK for a backtest: revaluation at the 0.25 % floor (IRP, 2013 reform) vs CPI in 2014-2018, cumulative real loss and any official estimate of savings in % of GDP.
items.hints: BOE revaluation decrees 2014-2017, INE CPI, AIReF / Banco de España / FEDEA on the IRP; AR2015/AR2018 country fiche Spain.

parameter.name: deuda_2034_sin_cambios
parameter.unit: % del PIB

items.need: BENCHMARK: European Commission Debt Sustainability Monitor 2024 (or 2025 if published) no-policy-change baseline for Spain: gross public debt in % of GDP in 2034 (and 2030), plus the assumed structural primary balance.
items.hints: economy-finance.ec.europa.eu Debt Sustainability Monitor 2024 (Institutional Paper), country annex Spain (statistical table).

parameter.name: elasticidad_producto_empleo
parameter.unit: % de PIB potencial por 1 % de empleo

items.need: Output elasticity of labour in the European Commission production function used for potential GDP (and so in the Ageing Report): the labour share alpha in the Cobb-Douglas Y = TFP * L^alpha * K^(1-alpha). Model use: GDP deviation from extra employment = alpha x employment deviation.
items.hints: Havik et al. (2014), 'The Production Function Methodology for Calculating Potential Growth Rates & Output Gaps', European Economy Economic Papers 535; Blondeau et al. (2021) Discussion Paper 150 update.

parameter.name: cuota_iva_general
parameter.unit: fracción del gasto de consumo (cesta del IPC) gravada al tipo general

items.need: Share of household consumption (CPI/HICP basket weights) taxed at the 21 % standard VAT rate in Spain (rest at 10 %, 4 %, exempt). Derive from INE CPI weights by VAT rate or from the 2012 INE note (IPC a impuestos constantes) or AEAT/EC VAT studies.
items.hints: INE IPC ponderaciones; INE note September 2012 https://www.ine.es/daco/daco42/daco421/ipc0912.pdf; EC 'VAT rates applied in the Member States'; AIReF spending review on tax benefits (beneficios fiscales IVA).

parameter.name: recaudacion_por_punto_irpf
parameter.unit: % del PIB por 1 pp en todos los tramos del IRPF

items.need: Static revenue from raising every bracket of the IRPF general scale (state + regional) by 1 pp, in % of GDP. Derive from the latest AEAT 'Estadística de los declarantes del IRPF' (2023 returns): sum of base liquidable general (and the savings base if you include it, say which) minus the personal and family minimum actually applied (mínimo personal y familiar), times 0.01, divided by nominal GDP of that year (2023 ≈ 1,498,324 M EUR). Model use: revenue = this × pp.

parameter.name: recaudacion_por_punto_irpf_alto
parameter.unit: % del PIB por 1 pp en la base liquidable por encima de 60.000 €

items.need: Static revenue from +1 pp on the part of the general taxable base above 60,000 EUR (top state+regional bracket starts at 60,000 for the state scale): sum over filers of max(0, base liquidable general − 60,000) × 0.01 / GDP. AEAT publishes declarants by tramos of base imponible/liquidable with amounts: use the brackets above 60,000 (count and total base) and say the approximation. extra_parameters pareto_a_alto = mean base above 60,000 / (mean − 60,000) from the same table.

parameter.name: eti_general
parameter.unit: elasticidad de la renta gravable al neto de impuestos (1 − tipo marginal), todos los contribuyentes

items.need: Elasticity of taxable income (ETI) with respect to the net-of-tax rate for Spanish taxpayers overall. Spanish estimates: Sanmartín (2007, Hacienda Pública Española / Review of Public Economics) on the 1999 reform; Díaz-Caro & Onrubia (2018); Almunia & López-Rodríguez (2019?) bunching; international: Saez, Slemrod & Giertz (2012, JEL) survey (0.12-0.40). Model use: revenue offset = ETI × m/(1−m) × static change, m ≈ average marginal rate.

parameter.name: eti_alta
parameter.unit: elasticidad de la renta gravable al neto de impuestos, rentas altas

items.need: ETI for high incomes (top brackets) in Spain or comparable countries; this is contested (high values in the US, low in Europe): give a debate with at least two schools and sources. Model use: offset on the top-rate lever = ETI_top × m_top/(1−m_top) × a (Pareto parameter).

parameter.name: cuota_base_irpf_20_superior
parameter.unit: % de la base liquidable (o renta) del 20 % de declarantes con más renta

items.need: VALIDATION benchmark: share of total base liquidable (or of total gross income declared) accounted for by the 20 % of declarants with the highest income, latest AEAT year (also top 10 % in derivation). AEAT tables by deciles/tramos.

parameter.name: recaudacion_por_punto_iva_reducido
parameter.unit: % del PIB por 1 pp del tipo reducido (10 %)

items.need: Static VAT revenue from +1 pp of the 10 % reduced rate, in % of GDP. The 2012 hike (8 -> 10 %) is a Spanish test: AEAT Informe Anual de Recaudación Tributaria 2012/2013 splits the effect of the rate changes; a previously verified card found 9,701 M EUR a year for the 2012 rise of all rates (standard 18->21, reduced 8->10) and 2,883 M per pp of the standard rate. Divide by GDP of the year (2013 ≈ 1,025,652 M EUR... use the year of the revenue).

parameter.name: recaudacion_por_punto_sociedades
parameter.unit: % del PIB por 1 pp del tipo nominal del Impuesto sobre Sociedades

items.need: Static revenue from +1 pp of the nominal Impuesto sobre Sociedades rate (25 %), in % of GDP: AEAT 'Estadística de las declaraciones del Impuesto sobre Sociedades' (base imponible positiva, cuota íntegra, tipo efectivo) latest year; per pp ≈ 1 % × taxable base (note deductions keep effective rates lower). extra_parameters semielasticidad_base_sociedades: semi-elasticity of reported profits to the tax rate (Heckemeyer & Overesch 2017 meta-analysis, about 0.8 % per pp; or Spanish evidence).

parameter.name: traslado_sociedades_salarios
parameter.unit: fracción del Impuesto sobre Sociedades que acaba en menores salarios, largo plazo

items.need: Long-run share of the corporate income tax borne by workers through lower wages. Contested: Fuest, Peichl & Siegloch (2018, AER, Germany: about 51 %); Arulampalam, Devereux & Maffini (2012, EER: 49 %); US agencies (CBO/JCT 25 %, Treasury 18-21 %); Spanish evidence if any. Give a debate with schools.

parameter.name: salarios_pib
parameter.unit: % del PIB: sueldos y salarios brutos (D11)

items.need: Wages and salaries (ESA D11) in % of GDP, Spain, 2024 (Eurostat nama_10_gdp, unit PC_GDP or CP_MEUR / B1GQ). Use: python3 -m scripts.voting_aid_impacts_kit eurostat nama_10_gdp "geo=ES&na_item=D11&na_item=B1GQ&unit=CP_MEUR&sinceTimePeriod=2023". Accounting, grade A.
